quote: We present a neural model that ... generates navigation instructions that contain salient landmarks, learned directly from human natural language instructions.

We present a neural model that takes a real‑world map representation from OpenStreetMap as input and generates navigation instructions that contain salient landmarks, learned directly from human natural language instructions…
The task addressed in our work is that of automatically generating Natural Language Landmark Navigation Instructions (NLLNI) from realworld open-source geographical data from OpenStreetMap.
datasets: 7,672 instances of routes in OpenStreetMap and corresponding crowd-sourced natural language instructions
outputs: natural language route instructions containing landmarks
natural language route instructions that contain salient landmarks

BLEU is calculated with SacreBLEU on lower‑cased and tokenized text. Length is the average length in number of tokens. Landmarks is the number of landmark occurrences per instance… SDTW is success weighted by normalized Dynamic Time Warping. SR is the first try success rate… SNT is success weighted by navigation time.

quote: Each generated navigation instruction was validated by another human crowdsourcing worker who had to reach the goal location by following the instruction on Google Street View.

If one of two annotators did so successfully, the navigation instructions were considered valid… The task is successful if the annotator stops the run within a 25 meter radius around the goal location.

Another annotator will later read your instructions in order to find the goal location in StreetView (Navigation Run Task). If the other annotator successfully navigates to the goal location, your instruction is validated.
guideline: The task is successful if the annotator stops the run within a 25 meter radius around the goal location.

Human annotators (via Amazon Mechanical Turk) are asked to follow the generated navigation instructions in Google Street View and stop when they believe the goal is reached; success is defined by proximity to the true goal.
The task is successful if the annotator stops the run within a 25 meter radius around the goal location.
